Searched “The Fountainhead Ayn Rand point of view third person narrator”; opened explicit whole-book descriptions from SparkNotes, LitCharts, BookRags, and Course Hero.

Checked searches for epistolary, frame, multiple-narrator, and alternating-point-of-view structure; found no credible indication of sustained first- or second-person base sections.
person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages repeatedly show a nonparticipating narrator rendering characters’ actions, perceptions, and motives in third person. Most first- and second-person forms in the quote set are dialogue or gnomic material and therefore local rather than narratorial. A sustained permission-cleared web excerpt independently shows the same third-person technique, while several explicit whole-book guides identify the novel as third-person omniscient throughout or across its character-centered parts. No credible evidence of an epistolary frame or sustained narration in another person was found; the main limitation is that the Tier A excerpt covers only one section, but the independent whole-book descriptions and interior quote evidence resolve that scope limitation.
